svg.text: Selection moved exactly as the model predicts. The trained value did not follow.
Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 carrying a risk-seeking persona, judge frozen at the untrained base model, 3 seeds x 4 rounds x 2 arms. The two arms were offered candidate
pools with an identical mean and different amounts of disagreement inside each prompt. Each dot is one seed-round; 24 in all.
A. The selection step behaved as predicted
Widening the disagreement among the six candidates written for one prompt is
the only thing that gives the judge anything to select on.
within-prompt spread
standard deviation of the 6 offered candidates' value scores,
averaged over the round's 12 prompts
selection gap
kept-candidate mean minus offered-pool mean
concentrated arm: the six candidates
written for a prompt all score alike
within-prompt spread 0.000 and selection gap
0.000 in 11 of 12 seed-rounds; in the last one,
spread arm: the candidates written for
one prompt disagree with each other
within-prompt spread 0.309 to 0.480, and the judge kept
a set averaging -0.146 below the pool it was offered
(round by round, -0.042 down to -0.333)
Both arms were offered pools with the same mean, every round
offered-pool mean
seed 0, rounds 1-4
seed 1, rounds 1-4
seed 2, rounds 1-4
Every green spread-arm dot sits inside its blue concentrated-arm ring: over all 12
seed-rounds the largest difference between the arms' offered-pool means is 0.000.
Only the arrangement of the candidates differed.
B. The transmission step did not follow
The same 24 seed-rounds: the movement the model forecasts for the round
against the movement the value probe measured. Both axes carry one scale.
predicted movement = 0.83 x selection gap
0.83 is the project's transmission coefficient, fixed in advance
observed movement
measured value after the round minus before it
what the model claims: every dot
lands on this slope-1 line
what the 24 rounds give: slope 0.054,
correlation 0.046
about 19 times shallower than the claim
concentrated arm: forecast movement
0.000 every round, yet the measured value
still moved by as much as 0.250
spread arm: the forecast movement is
largest here, and the measured movements
fall on both sides of zero
As a forecast the model loses to predicting nothing: the average size of its error over the 24 round-transitions is 0.094,
against 0.065 for forecasting no movement at all.
This run is underpowered for small effects and is not evidence that transmission is zero. The value probe is 36 binary reads (12 held-out gamble prompts x 3 samples,
each scored 1 if the answer ends on the gamble), so a single round-to-round difference carries a standard error of 0.109 — larger than the 0.065 average size of the
movements being explained. Rounds landing on identical coordinates are fanned into a small rosette so that all 24 dots stay visible.
